$comment: Fables Stage 1 binding spec. Builders complete scenarios 2-6 to the depth of scenario 1 (canonical example). Output file: deliverables/rule-tree.nsw.v1.complete.json. No numeric fault percentage may be assigned to the user's case anywhere in this structure.

field_notes.rule_citations: Array of { rule: 'r126', title: string }. Use corrected numbers: r126, r72, r73, r114, r148, r149, r296. r71 and r298 are PROHIBITED (wrong citations in source doc).
field_notes.classification_questions: Ordered array of { id, slot, question_voice, question_web, answer_type, options?, validation, reprompt_max: 2 }
field_notes.exceptions: Array of { id, probe_question, slot, effect: 'downgrade_band' | 'flag_unclear' | 'escalate' }
field_notes.band_logic: Deterministic mapping from (pattern_match, exceptions_present[], damage_consistent) to one of: likely | possible | unclear | insufficient. No other values permitted. No numeric field exists in this schema by design — do not add one.
field_notes.outputs: One entry per band: { band, text_voice, text_web }. Every text must end by attaching disclaimer key 'master' (reference, not inline copy). Text must obey framing_rules in disclaimers spec.
field_notes.escalation_overrides: Conditions within this scenario that bypass band output entirely and route to human (in addition to the 7 global triggers).

global_escalation_triggers.note: serious -> immediate, before any further slots; minor -> complete safety check then escalate

global_escalation_triggers.condition: fraud signals: story inconsistency, rego mismatch, third-party pressure
customer explicitly disputes the AI's summary
customer asks for legal advice directly
global_escalation_triggers.note: deflect with persona utterance category (e), then offer callback; do not answer

rule_citations.title: Keeping a safe distance behind vehicles

classification_questions.question_voice: Were you the vehicle in front, or the vehicle behind?
classification_questions.question_web: In the collision, your vehicle was:

classification_questions.question_voice: Just before the impact, was your vehicle stopped or moving?
classification_questions.question_web: Just before impact, your vehicle was:

classification_questions.question_voice: How many vehicles were involved altogether?
classification_questions.validation: >=2; if >=3 route to s6 and check esc-multiparty

default_pattern.description: Following driver usually responsible for maintaining safe gap (r126)

exceptions.probe_question: Did the vehicle in front brake suddenly without an apparent reason?
As far as you know, were the front vehicle's brake lights working?
Did the vehicle in front reverse into you?
Was this part of a chain collision — were you pushed into the vehicle ahead?

damage_consistency_check.expected: rear damage on front vehicle AND front damage on rear vehicle

band_logic.when: pattern matched AND no exceptions AND damage consistent
pattern matched AND >=1 exception unconfirmed or present
any flag_unclear exception OR damage inconsistent

outputs.text_voice: In most rear-end collisions in New South Wales, the driver of the following vehicle is considered responsible for keeping a safe gap. Based on what you've told me, your situation looks like a common example of that pattern — but whether it applies depends on the full evidence. {{ATTACH:master}}
outputs.text_web: In most rear-end collisions in NSW, the following driver is considered responsible for maintaining a safe following distance (Road Rule 126). Your description matches this common pattern. Whether it applies here depends on the full evidence. {{ATTACH:master}}

outputs.text_voice: Rear-end collisions in New South Wales usually involve the following driver's duty to keep a safe gap, but you've mentioned something that can change how these are assessed. A lawyer will need to look at the details. {{ATTACH:master}}
outputs.text_web: This matches the common rear-end pattern under NSW Road Rule 126, but one or more factors you've described (such as sudden braking or brake-light issues) can affect how these collisions are assessed. {{ATTACH:master}}

outputs.text_voice: Based on what you've described, this doesn't fit the usual rear-end pattern neatly, so I won't guess. The details you've given me will go straight to a lawyer to review properly. {{ATTACH:master}}
outputs.text_web: Your description doesn't fit the standard rear-end pattern neatly — for example the damage locations or sequence of events raise questions. This is exactly the kind of situation a lawyer should review. {{ATTACH:master}}

outputs.text_voice: I don't have quite enough detail to tell you how collisions like this are usually understood. That's completely fine — a lawyer will go through it with you. {{ATTACH:master}}
outputs.text_web: There isn't enough information yet to match your accident to a common pattern. A lawyer will review what you've provided and follow up. {{ATTACH:master}}

rule_citations.title: Giving way at an intersection with a give way sign or line

seed.default_pattern: driver on terminating road gives way
seed.seed_output: NSW rules generally require the driver joining from a terminating road to give way. This may not apply if visibility was obscured or both vehicles entered at the same moment.

rule_citations.title: Giving way when entering or driving in a roundabout

seed.default_pattern: entering driver gives way to circulating traffic
seed.seed_output: At a roundabout in NSW, vehicles entering must give way to vehicles already in the roundabout. Multi-lane roundabout conflicts can be more complex.

rule_citations.title: Giving way when moving between marked lanes
Giving way when lines of traffic merge (zip merge)

seed.default_pattern: driver crossing marked lines gives way; zip merge: vehicle ahead has priority
seed.seed_output: Changing lanes requires giving way to vehicles already in the destination lane. In a zip merge, the vehicle ahead has priority — this is a common source of dispute.

rule_citations.title: Reversing — driver must not reverse unless safe

seed.default_pattern: reversing driver must ensure path is clear
exceptions: stationary vehicle struck in car park
seed.seed_output: A driver reversing must ensure the path is clear. Car park collisions are a frequent exception where fault is genuinely shared.

rule_citations.title: Keeping a safe distance behind vehicles

seed.default_pattern: compare each driver's departure from standard care; outcomes often split between parties
seed.seed_output: Multi-vehicle collisions in NSW are often split between the parties involved, depending on the evidence. A lawyer will assess how that applies to your situation.
seed.note: Seed output rewritten from source doc: the original quoted 60/40, 70/30, 100% figures. General split outcomes may be described qualitatively only — never quote percentages to the user about their case, and avoid numeric examples in customer-facing text.
